content:
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon, especially after low points; adjust upward by 5–10% for such periods.
- Overestimates early in the 30-day forecast, particularly when sentiment is neutral or flat; reduce initial forecast values by 3–5%.
- Shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often overshoot peaks and fail to capture sustained rallies; apply dampening factor for 3rd+ day after spike.
- When sentiment history is all 0.00 (neutral), model exhibits high lag — delay in recognizing true trend direction; add 1–2 day lag correction for price momentum.
- In absence of event context, model overreacts to recent volatility; suppress forecast volatility if no official event is active.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period corrections — add 2–3% buffer to forecast at 25–30 day mark to account for mean reversion.
